messages:
sanjay: Heads up — eu-west-2 GPU capacity alarm. ~120 pods Pending, most are `Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu` or stuck on scheduling windows. Cluster-autoscaler is showing scale-up requests but not converging. Can folks jump in? :eyes:

maya: On it. Any signs of ENI or subnet IP exhaustion? That often looks similar.

liam: autoscaler logs show a bunch of FailedScaleUp: "No capacity found for instance type" and also API rate limit 429s when trying to create nodes. Also seeing a few tainted nodegroups (training-* taints) that prod can't land on.

sanjay: I pulled a quick kubectl for the Pending list: 
```
kubectl get pods -n prod -o wide | grep Pending | head
prod-api-5f7b9   0/1 Pending   0   5m   (0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu)
training-job-202  0/1 Pending   0   3m   (0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate)
```

sarah: Looks like two problems: spot churn + a priorityclass mismatch. Training pool is using a high-priorityclass accidentally, so autoscaler thinks those are important and competes with prod. We should demote training jobs first.

jordan: We also have the on-demand fallback pool configured but it's at 0 desired because of cost guardrails. I can flip it to +4 on-demand nodes for immediate relief if ops-ok. That should accept prod pods right away.

maya: Quick mitigation plan: 1) cordon training nodepool, 2) patch training pods to use lower PriorityClass OR scale down the training job controller, 3) temporarily raise on-demand fallback desired to 4, 4) set cluster-autoscaler exponential backoff relaxed (short), 5) open ticket to review api rate limit retries.

liam: Commands I ran / propose: 
```
# cordon training nodepool (kube label selector)
kubectl get nodes -l nodepool=training -o name | xargs -n1 kubectl cordon
# emergency scale on-demand group via terraform pipeline (ops-run)
ops run terraform apply -var 'od_desired=4' --target=module.on_demand_pool
# patch training priority
kubectl patch job training-batch-123 -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"priorityClassName":"low-priority"}}}}'
```

ops-bot: alert: gpu_nodepool_utilization eu-west-2 > 95% (sustained 6m). Paging infra-oncall.

sanjay: I'm starting the on-demand increase and cordoning training now. Also toggling CA backoff values so we try again faster. Jordan — please confirm when on-demand nodes show Registered.

jordan: applying now. ETA ~90s for nodes to register (warmed AMI, on-demand).

sarah: I'll queue a quick K8s admission webhook check to prevent accidental high-priorityclass on training jobs in future. Also adding a guard in the training job controller to refuse priority > medium.

liam: After nodes come up, watch for long provisioning times (driver install/taints). We should have a bootstrap hook to mark gpu-ready via a node condition so CA knows capacity.

sanjay: Update: on-demand nodes registered at 1755554323. Seeing ~40 pods schedule immediately (prod wins). Pending dropped to ~80. Keep cordoned + scale actions in place.

jordan: will leave on-demand at +4 for 2 hours and then roll down if healthy. Filing a follow-up change to add a small reserved on-demand buffer for eu-west-2 to avoid flapping.

maya: Action items: - revert training priority / enforce controller guard - tune CA rate limit/retry logic and add jitter - reserve a small on-demand emergency pool + document cost threshold - add alert for priority inversion (when low-priority pods have priority >= prod).

sanjay: Thanks all. Logging incident and creating ticket INF-4237 for postmortem + cost impact. If anything regresses ping here.

sarah: Also note: we saw one spot node drain that triggered a cascade because preemption went after the wrong PriorityClass — adding to postmortem.

ops-bot: incident INF-4237 created by sanjay. Severity: sev3.

liam: I'll follow up with CAP team on CA config and API rate limiting patterns.

sanjay: closing thread for now — will reopen if Pending > 50 again. :white_check_mark:
